newsitem.title: USA: CBO sees $11 bln U.S. deficit first 9 months FY97.
newsitem.headline: CBO sees $11 bln U.S. deficit first 9 months FY97.

text.p: The U.S. budget deficit is expected to fall to $11 billion for the first nine months of fiscal 1997, down sharply from a $74 billion deficit in the same period last year, according to a Congressional Budget Office (CBO) analysis obtained Thursday.
The analysis, dated July 9, was based on the May Treasury statement of government revenues and spending. CBO estimated a $54 billion surplus for the month of June.
"Receipts continued to be quite strong in May and June, while outlay growth slowed," the analysis said. Fiscal 1997 started October 1, 1996, and ends September 30, 1997.

"A $54 billion surplus is estimated for June, lowering the cumulative deficit for the first nine months of fiscal year 1997 to $11 billion, down sharply from the $74 billion deficit last year for the same period," the analysis said.
Wall Street analysts have forecast the deficit could fall below $50 billion by the end of fiscal 1997.
Congress is currently in the last stages of putting together legislation to implement a five-year budget agreement that aims to wipe out the deficit by the year 2002.
White House Budget Director Franklin Raines said Wednesday that despite an improvement in the deficit this year due to a strong economy, the budget agreement is still needed to erase the deficit.
